title: 18 Canadians collect at least 1 point in 10-0 rout of host Denmark at women's hockey worlds
summary: Eve Gascon stopped all 11 shots she faced as Canada blanked Japan 9-0 at the women's hockey world championship in Herning, Denmark, on Sunday.

image.caption: Sophie Jaques, middle, was among the Canadian players with two assists in Monday's game. Chloe Primerano, Caitlin Kraemer, and Ella Shelton were the others. (Ida Marie Odgaard/Ritzau Scanpix via Associated Press)

blocks.text: Eve Gascon stopped all 11 shots she faced as Canada blanked Japan 9-0 at the women's hockey world championship in Herning, Denmark, on Sunday.
Emma Maltais, Laura Stacey lead way as Canada outshoots opponent 74-6
Emma Maltais scored twice, Laura Stacey had a goal and two assists, and Canada remained undefeated at the word women's hockey championship with a 10-0 rout of host Denmark on Monday in Herning.
Jessie Eldridge and Sarah Fillier had a goal and an assist for Canada, while Kendall Cooper, Sara Manness, Renata Fast, Rosalie Tremblay and Kristin O'Neill also scored.
Sophie Jaques, Chloe Primerano, Caitlin Kraemer, and Ella Shelton each had two assists as 18 of Canada's 20 skaters registered at least a point.
Kayle Osborne made six saves for Canada, which outshot the Danes 74-6 and leads Group A on nine points from three regulation wins.

blocks.text: Caroline Bjergstad surrendered six goals on 41 shots before giving way to Aya Juhl Petersen midway through the second period. Petersen allowed four goals on 33 shots in relief.
Canada ends group play Wednesday against Finland.
Caroline Harvey scored a hat trick and the defending champion the United States routed Austria 11-1 in Esbjerg.
The last goal of the game by Austria was the first conceded in three games by the U.S., which has scored 23 so far.

Tessa Janecke scored twice and had an assist, captain Hilary Knight netted twice, Joy Dunne had a goal and three assists, and Rory Guilday, Lacey Eden, and Megan Keller each contributed one goal and an assist.

blocks.text: Harvey scored two of the opening period’s four goals and completed her hat trick in the third after registering five assists in the previous two games. She had another assist on Monday.
Knight was fed in front of the goal by Cayla Barnes to increase the lead to 2-0 and her second made it 9-0 to improve her record tally at the worlds to 70 goals in 90 games.
The U.S. pulled goalie Aerin Frankel 10:45 into the middle period when she had just two saves and the score was 6-0. Gwyneth Philips came on.
Annika Fazokas scored the consolation for Austria, which met the U.S. for the first time in its first appearance in the top division.
In the final preliminary game on Wednesday, the Americans face the Czech Republic.
